subject: com.netflix.kayenta.sql.storage.model.SqlBaseObject(id)
rationale: ORM @Id on SqlBaseObject.id (inherited by all four entities). Exercised through canary_config and canary_archive: duplicate-id creates were rejected by application existence checks with HTTP 400 (no INSERT issued); PUT with an existing id caused Hibernate merge -> 'update ... where id=?' and read-back shows exactly one row, i.e. id identifies the persistent row.

subject: canary_archive(id)
rationale: canary_archive.id has length 255. The id is client-controlled via POST /canaryResultArchive (query param pipelineId). A 255-character id was persisted (read-back CHAR_LENGTH=255). A 256-character id passed all application checks, Hibernate issued 'insert into canary_archive', and MySQL (strict mode) rejected it with SQL Error 1406/22001 'Data too long for column id'; Spring translated it to DataIntegrityViolationException and kork's generic handler returned HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error' exposing the exception class. Read-back shows no row persisted. The application has no length validation.
limitations: Behaviour depends on MySQL STRICT_TRANS_TABLES (enabled, default); non-strict MySQL would silently truncate.

subject: canary_archive(content)

limitations: A null domain object would serialize to the JSON text 'null', not SQL NULL, so the column predicate is unreachable from the API.
